title: Countable unions of at most countable sets
statement: A subset is at most countable when its underlying type is countable in the sense of [def-sfb-countable-set], that is, it admits an injection into $\mathbf N$. Let $X$ and $I$ be sets, $S\subseteq I$ an at most countable subset, and $(B_i)_{i\in S}$ a family of at most countable subsets of $X$. Then $\bigcup_{i\in S}B_i$ is at most countable. For every sequence $(T_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ of at most countable subsets of $X$, the union $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbf N}T_n$ is at most countable. For any two at most countable subsets $U,V\subseteq X$, the union $U\cup V$ is at most countable.
